claims.text: Narrowing the distribution of oxidation states at transition-metal active sites will enhance product selectivity relative to a broader distribution.
Narrowing the distribution of oxidation states at transition-metal active sites will enhance catalyst durability relative to a broader distribution.
A narrower oxidation-state distribution produces a more uniform local electronic environment.
A more uniform electronic environment produces more consistent and optimal adsorbate binding.
Local electronic structure affects adsorbate binding at transition-metal active sites.
The distribution of adsorption energies can govern catalytic behavior.
More consistent adsorbate binding reduces undesired side reactions and thereby enhances selectivity.
Avoiding localized overactivity or inadequate binding minimizes active-site degradation and thereby enhances durability.
As-synthesized transition-metal catalysts can possess a broad distribution of oxidation states at their active sites.
A post-synthesis thermal or chemical treatment can narrow the oxidation-state distribution without changing particle size, morphology, or support composition.
Operando XPS/XAS can quantify the narrowing or variance of the active-site oxidation-state distribution.
The proposed effect should apply primarily when electronic-structure variation, rather than morphology, governs adsorbate interactions.
The magnitude of selectivity and durability improvement may depend on catalyst composition and reaction type.
Under otherwise identical conditions, the treated catalyst should show statistically significant improvements in selectivity and operational durability.
